title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop affects verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single LLM proposal produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared LLM proposal validated by a deterministic netops verifier and subjected to up to one automated repair iteration if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test was implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01); with n = 1 and n10 = 1 the archived two-sided p = 1.00 under that convention. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; measured marginal verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though the verifier corrected at least one concrete baseline failure. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction:
Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly being explored for network operations (NetOps) tasks including intent parsing, configuration synthesis, change planning, and limited self-healing. Practitioners and researchers emphasize that operational safety for LLM-driven NetOps depends less on any single component and more on engineering around the model: deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback are commonly recommended [1,2,3]. The canonical operational pattern is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): the model generates a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks formalized properties, and automated repairs or human review resolve violations.

Despite this consensus, quantitative measurements that isolate the verifier’s marginal contribution while holding model proposals fixed are scarce. This gap leaves uncertainty about the expected incremental return from introducing a verifier (and a modest automated repair budget) when the LLM already produces high-quality candidates. To fill that niche we preregistered and executed a paired experiment that answers a narrowly scoped operational question: given identical initial proposals (shared_initial_candidate semantics), how much does integrating a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair iteration reduce verifier-detected safety violations relative to the same LLM alone? Our design preserves the LLM’s single proposal for both arms so the measured effect is attributable only to verification and a constrained repair stage.
sections.related_work:
Deterministic network-configuration verification has a long history in systems and formal-methods research. Classical header-space and route-model verifiers and subsequent Batfish-inspired tools can check reachability, isolation, and update-safety properties and have demonstrated the ability to catch subtle misconfigurations pre-deployment [4]. In parallel, recent NetOps and AIOps literature documents LLM-based intent→configuration systems and argues for operational guardrails; agentic-NetOps architectures integrate LLMs with components that provide deterministic checks and operational controls [1,2]. Generate–validate–repair patterns are also common in structured generation and safety-critical generation tasks, where a verifier or critic is used to filter or correct model outputs [5]. Separate bodies of work document systemic failure modes of LLM-driven automation (hallucination, overconfidence, tool-integration errors) and recommend layered defenses including deterministic analyzers and human oversight [6,7].

What is less represented in prior work is a preregistered, artifact-backed ablation that quantifies the marginal verifier effect with matched initial proposals. Existing systems papers report architectures or combined end-to-end performance; they do not, in the supplied literature set, provide controlled paired comparisons that keep the model output identical across arms to isolate verifier+repair impact. This study contributes that controlled, evidence-backed measurement and situates its conditional findings relative to the verification and agentic-NetOps literature [1,2,4,5].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and inferential plan. We preregistered the study (study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026) and fixed inclusion rules, random seeds, estimands, analysis code, multiplicity handling, and a stopping rule before observing outcomes. The primary confirmatory hypothesis compared paired binary outcomes (success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations) between baseline and guarded conditions. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the preregistered confirmatory test was a McNemar two-sided exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs implementation with alpha=0.05.

Task corpus and stratification. We used a deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks generated with fixed seeds and stratified into three intent clusters: VLAN-change (167), ACL-change (167), and static-route-change (166). To align with verifier scope the task payloads were constrained to a small feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}); tasks referencing unmodeled features were excluded by preregistered rules and routed to an excluded cohort (none occurred in the confirmatory set).

Generation semantics and experimental control. To isolate the verifier marginal effect we used shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each task a single LLM proposal was produced and that identical text served as the baseline proposal and as input to the guarded arm. The guarded arm ran the deterministic verifier on that shared candidate and invoked at most one automated repair iteration only when the verifier flagged a preregistered high- or medium-severity violation. This prevents conflation with verifier-guided regeneration and isolates verification-plus-repair applied to the same initial candidate.

Modeling, verifier and repair. The requested LLM was gpt-5-mini (via a hosted adapter) with a single-attempt generation and a 2000-token output cap. The deterministic verifier was a purpose-built netops validator mapping concrete violation codes to severity levels; pass/fail in the primary outcome is defined relative to that validator’s coverage. The repair budget was constrained by the adapter to at most one automated repair attempt per task when a preregistered severe violation occurred. Repair prompts and repair responses were archived for each attempted repair.

Confirmatory inference and resampling. The preregistered confirmatory test was an exact McNemar two-sided test implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01) with two-sided p computed by doubling the smaller tail probability and truncating at 1.0. We also computed paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence intervals for the absolute paired difference using B = 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729, preserving pairing during resampling. Resampling unit = task/pair.

Operational controls. The preregistered retry policy permitted a small number of automated retries for transient provider errors; execution stopped after processing the preregistered confirmatory pairs. We recorded model-call accounting, repair-stage calls, and all per-task validator diagnostics. All design choices and analysis code are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic reproduction.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes. The run processed 500 complete paired tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Observed model-call accounting shows 501 hosted-model calls: 500 shared-initial generations and 1 repair-stage call. Aggregated per-condition results: baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Pairwise contingency counts: n11 = 499 (both pass), n10 = 1 (guarded pass only), n01 = 0 (baseline pass only), n00 = 0 (both fail). The absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Inferential results and uncertainty. Under the preregistered exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention the two-sided McNemar p-value for n = 1 (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) is p = 1.00. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). These numbers were produced by the registered analysis executor and are reported without post hoc adjustments. The small number of discordant pairs drives low statistical sensitivity: the preregistered power calculation had assumed a substantially higher baseline failure prevalence (~30%), but the observed prevalence (1/500) induced a ceiling effect that reduces the ability to detect modest absolute improvements.

Repair activity and discordant-episode provenance. The guarded arm invoked a single repair-stage call; that repair produced the single discordant outcome (the task where the baseline failed and the guarded arm passed). Execution accounting (model_calls_used = 501; observed repair-stage calls = 1) and per-task validator traces confirm exactly one corrected episode in the confirmatory set. Validator diagnostics and the repair transcript for that episode are archived and identify the specific violation code the verifier reported and the repair content produced by the automated repair attempt.

Secondary analyses and diagnostics. Preplanned secondary per-violation-class analyses were uninformative due to near-zero counts: with only one discordant episode there is insufficient data to estimate reliable per-class risk reductions. Inspection of representative per-task validator traces shows many tasks (including medium- and hard-pattern examples) where the shared candidate met all verifier-modeled constraints and no repair was attempted. Representative artifact examples illustrating validator diagnostics, normalized configurations, and difficulty metadata are included in the evidence bundle.
sections.discussion:
Conditional interpretation and operational meaning. Within the constrained experimental regime — single requested LLM (gpt-5-mini requested), shared_initial_candidate semantics, a deterministic verifier modeling a limited feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), and at most one automated repair iteration — the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals on verifier-scoped properties and the measured marginal pass-rate benefit of adding the verifier was small (0.002). This is a conditional, operationally framed measurement: when baseline proposal quality is already very high for the verifier’s modeled properties, modest verifier+repair budgets yield limited measurable gains on a composite pass/fail metric, yet can still remediate rare concrete failures as observed here.

Statistical nuance. The archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the preregistered exact-binomial convention applied to a single discordant pair. Exact small-sample p-values can be non-intuitive; here p = 1.00 indicates that the observed discordant-pattern is not statistically surprising under the null when only one discordant pair exists. The paired-bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.006] complements the p-value by quantifying sampling variability for the absolute paired difference. Together they communicate a small point estimate improvement with wide relative uncertainty driven by a ceiling effect.

Design trade-offs and deployment implications. The shared_initial_candidate semantics purposely measure marginal verifier benefit in deployments that constrain regeneration (to preserve proposals for human review or to reduce model-call cost). This design minimizes model calls (observed model_calls_used = 501) and keeps the original proposal intact for human operators, but it forgoes potential gains from verifier-informed regeneration. Alternative operational choices — allowing verifier-guided regeneration, increasing the repair iteration budget, or applying broader verifier coverage — may increase final pass probability at additional model-call, latency, and engineering cost. Practitioners should therefore measure baseline error prevalence on representative operational data and align verifier coverage with operator-critical constraints before investing in repair budgets: extremely low baseline error rates limit marginal return on modest verifier+repair investments.

Failure modes and diagnostics. The study highlights two complementary failure-mode observations supported by the artifacts. First, when verifier-modeled constraints are within the LLM’s training/generalization envelope and task inputs are constrained, LLM-only proposals can be highly reliable on those properties. Second, deterministic validators can still provide operational value by catching and enabling correction of rare but concrete failures; the single corrected episode in this run is an existence proof of that remediation path. Both points are narrowly scoped to verifier-modeled properties and the synthetic corpus; broader operational safety depends on verifier expressiveness and the range of operator-critical constraints [4,6].

Recommendations. (1) Empirically estimate baseline proposal error prevalence for verifier-scoped properties on representative workloads to inform budget decisions for verification and repair. (2) Expand verifier coverage to operator-critical constructs (vendor-specific CLI idiosyncrasies, stateful protocol behaviors) if those properties are important for deployment. (3) Match generation and repair semantics to deployment priorities: shared_initial_candidate minimizes model-call overhead and preserves proposals for human inspection; verifier-guided regeneration or larger repair budgets may improve final pass rates but at increased cost.
sections.conclusion: We report a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N = 500) isolating the verifier+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM produced near-ceiling verifier-scoped proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), giving an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the run’s exact-binomial convention). This conditional measurement demonstrates a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is already very high for the verifier-modeled properties and verifier coverage is limited, a modest verifier+repair budget can yield negligible measurable improvement on a composite pass/fail metric while still correcting rare concrete failures. Practitioners should estimate baseline verifier-scoped error prevalence, align verifier coverage with operational priorities, and choose generation/repair semantics that match deployment constraints. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call logs, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection of these claims.

limitations: Synthetic deterministic task corpus limited to the verifier-modeled features; task payloads were constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, wider cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or dynamic protocol states outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — we do not claim multi-model or cross-validator generality.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) induced a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the preregistered exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in the study evidence bundle. The run-level manifest and per-task scoring traces confirm exactly one such corrected episode in the confirmatory set.
